subject: Post-call: Clarify SSO / KMS / Log retention requirements and hosting path
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Sara Kim <sara@northridgehealth.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Clarify SSO / KMS / Log retention requirements and hosting path

Hi Sara — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align on whether Northridge needs Dedicated or Private deployment.

Recap of asks we noted on the call:
- SSO: Primary IdP = Okta; want SCIM + SAML for user provisioning and role mapping.
- KMS/HSM: Customer-managed keys required. Preference for HSM-backed keys (FIPS 140-2/3), ability to bring-your-own-key (BYOK) or integrate with Azure Key Vault/Thales/Entrust.
- Logs: 7-year retention for audit logs; encrypted-at-rest; ability to stream logs to your SIEM (Splunk) and an immutable copy in S3.
- Evidence: SOC2 artifacts + proof of key handling and attestation for HSM usage for regulated workflows.

Immediate asks from our side to proceed:
1) Can you confirm the HSM requirement: must keys live in a customer-controlled HSM (on-prem HSM or cloud HSM) vs. customer-managed keys in a cloud KMS?
2) Confirm the exact retention window (7 years confirmed?) and if retention applies to both application and access/audit logs.
3) Any network constraints for Private deployment (IP allowlists, egress controls, required peering) we should pre-load before a tech call?

Next steps we propose:
- Tech deep dive with our infra engineer (Aditya) to validate KMS patterns and logging pipeline (30–45 min).
- We will attach a brief deployment matrix that outlines tradeoffs between Hosted (with KMS connectors), Dedicated (reserved capacity + KMS integration), and Private (VPC or on-prem with HSM).
- Please share any internal security questionnaire sections that are blockers so we can pre-prepare evidence.

Attaching: northridge_kms_req.pdf (your upload) and our redwood-deployment-matrix.xlsx.

Thanks — I looped in Aditya to schedule the technical session.

—Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Sara Kim <sara@northridgehealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: security@northridgehealth.com, po+finance@northridgehealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Clarify SSO / KMS / Log retention requirements and hosting path

Thanks Mina — quick clarifications from our side so your team can scope the deep dive properly:

- KMS/HSM: Our security policy requires HSM-backed key material for PHI-related workloads. Ideally the HSM is customer-controlled. We can accept cloud HSM (Azure Dedicated HSM or AWS CloudHSM) if we retain key custodianship (BYOK with external key import or key wrapping).
- Retention: Yes, 7 years for audit events and access logs. Application-level usage logs can be retained for 1 year unless flagged for an incident. All logs must be encrypted and retain integrity proofs (we use SHA256 checksums in our pipeline).
- SIEM: We need Redwood to support streaming to our Splunk instance via syslog/HTTPS forwarder and provide proof-of-delivery (timestamps + checksums).
- Evidence: SOC2 Type II report is required; if using cloud HSM we need a vendor attestation for FIPS level. We also need a diagram showing where keys are stored and how decryption is gated.

On the hosting question: our default preference is to avoid on-prem physical HSMs (logistics), but if Redwood cannot provide a Private deployment with full network isolation and HSM integration, we will likely require Dedicated with a direct KMS connector + strict peering. Please outline the minimum controls that make Dedicated acceptable vs. when Private becomes mandatory.

Can we do the tech deep dive Wednesday morning (Nov 4) after 09:00 PT?

Sara Kim
VP Product, Northridge Health
sara@northridgehealth.com

On Wed, Nov 3, 2026 at 4:10 PM Sara Kim <sara@northridgehealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks Mina — quick clarifications from our side so your team can scope the deep dive properly:
> 
> - KMS/HSM: Our security policy requires HSM-backed key material for PHI-related workloads. Ideally the HSM is customer-controlled....

Thanks — this is very clear and helpful. Brief, high-level mapping so the tech call can focus on the gaps: 

Option A — Hosted API (our fastest path):
- Redwood hosts models and runtime. We can integrate with customer KMS (Azure Key Vault or AWS KMS) for envelope encryption, but the master key will still be managed by a cloud KMS provider.
- Pros: fastest onboarding, lower ops overhead.
- Cons: may not meet "customer-controlled HSM" interpretation if you require an on-prem or dedicated HSM instance.

Option B — Dedicated (reserved GPU pools):
- Dedicated capacity gives you tenant-isolated GPUs and VPC-level peering. We support direct KMS connectors (CloudHSM / Azure Dedicated HSM) and can route key operations through your KMS.
- Pros: strong isolation, meets most cloud-HSM BYOK patterns.
- Cons: still a cloud tenancy; some customers with strict hardware custody policies prefer Private.

Option C — Private (VPC or on-prem bundle):
- Full private control plane; can be deployed into your VPC or on-prem. Supports integration with on-prem HSMs or colocated cloud HSM appliances.
- Pros: highest control and easiest path to fully customer-controlled HSMs and network isolation.
- Cons: longer lead time and additional ops burden.

What we'll bring to the tech deep dive (Aditya will cover):
- KMS integration options and sample key flow diagrams (attached link).
- Logging pipeline: how we ship audit logs, TLS + checksum flows to Splunk, and retention lifecycle management.
- A checklist of evidence we can provide (SOC2, HSM vendor attestations, HSM import/export limitations).

Proposed times: Wed Nov 4 at 10:00 PT or Thu Nov 5 at 09:00 PT. Let me know what works and we' ll send a calendar invite with a short agenda.

—Mina
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sara / team — quick ops checklist ahead of the deep dive. If you can share these artifacts before the call it will make the session much more productive:

Required from Northridge before the call:
- Confirmed IdP metadata (Okta SAML metadata file) + SCIM provisioning scope.
- Exact HSM choice (Azure Dedicated HSM, AWS CloudHSM, or vendor name) and whether you require physical custody.
- Sample retention policy bullets that must be enforced (we have a template if helpful).
- Target Splunk ingest endpoint and auth method (TLS certificate or token).

What Redwood will bring / demonstrate:
- KMS integration patterns (BYOK, external key wrap, and HSM-backed flows) with sequence diagrams.
- Demo of log-forwarding pipeline to Splunk; how we produce immutable, timestamped chunks for long-term retention.
- Deployment matrix: minimal controls required to accept Dedicated vs. when Private is necessary.
- SOC2 and HSM vendor attestation examples (redacted).

Acceptance criteria for Dedicated vs Private (high level):
- Dedicated acceptable if: cloud-HSM integration + tenant isolation + VPC peering + ability to keep key custodianship via BYOK + contractual KMS SLAs.
- Private required if: physical custody of HSM is mandatory OR network isolation must prevent any shared-control plane dependencies.

Please drop the artifacts to the Drive link we shared or reply with a calendar time. Propose Wed Nov 4 10:00 PT — sending a tentative invite.

Thanks — Aditya
Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
